title: 5 ways AI Mode in Search helps you enjoy the real world
gist: Google promotes five AI Mode use cases framed around getting offline, but the substance is a roadmap of Search becoming an action layer: Personal Intelligence pulling Google Calendar context into answers, in-answer shopping with local stock checks and Google placing calls to stores, ticket discovery, Canvas generating runnable game simulations, and Canva rendering designs inside Search results. It also discloses first-party trend data, notably "how to digital detox" up 110% since the start of 2026.

insights.claim: Searches for "how to digital detox" are up 110% since the beginning of 2026 according to Google's own data, quantifying a measurable consumer pullback from screen time.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: A hard first-party number on anti-screen sentiment; relevant to engagement-dependent ad models and to the offline-experience economy.
insights.quote: questions like “how to digital detox” (+110% since the beginning of the year)
insights.locator: People are searching for more and more ways

insights.claim: "adult tennis lessons," "trail running," "hiking" and "run club" are all being searched more than ever before in 2026, pointing to sustained growth in participation sports and outdoor gear rather than a passing fad.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Supports demand for outdoor/athletic gear and local activity operators; a tailwind for footwear, apparel and experience-led retail.
insights.locator: This year, people are searching for “adult tennis lessons,”

insights.claim: Rising volume for "how to meet people my age near me" shows local social discovery is an unmet need being routed through a search box rather than through existing social networks.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Demand leaking to Search rather than social apps is a bearish signal for incumbent social platforms' relevance in real-world connection, and a whitespace for local community products.
insights.locator: “how to meet people my age near me”

themes.theme: Personal Intelligence as a data moat

insights.claim: Google has shipped "Personal Intelligence," which connects a user's Google apps so AI Mode responses are personalized — for example using connected Google Calendar availability to recommend cooking classes that fit next month's schedule.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Personalization grounded in Gmail/Calendar/Photos-scale personal data is a moat no standalone model vendor can replicate; it is the strongest structural argument for Google retaining assistant share.
insights.quote: Personal Intelligence allows you to securely connect the dots across your Google apps so that AI Mode’s responses are even more personalized to you.
insights.locator: Personal Intelligence allows you to securely

insights.claim: The feature is framed as opt-in and per-app ("if you've chosen to connect Google Calendar"), showing Google is gating its personal-data advantage behind explicit consent rather than turning it on by default.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Opt-in gating caps near-term attach rates and makes connection rate the key metric to watch for whether the data moat actually converts into product advantage.
insights.locator: For example, say you’re looking to get better at cooking

insights.claim: AI Mode now supports shopping inside the answer, including local stock checks when a query includes "nearby" or "near me," which requires Google to hold real-time local inventory data from retailers.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Real-time local inventory is the hard asset in the AI-shopping race; retailers that feed Google gain traffic, those that withhold get omitted from generated recommendations.
insights.locator: 2. Find the exact gear you need.

insights.claim: Google will place phone calls to nearby stores on the user's behalf to confirm product availability, extending agentic action from the web into offline retail operations.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Automated calling shifts inbound store labor onto retailers and gives Google inventory truth even where no data feed exists — a quiet structural advantage over marketplace competitors.
insights.quote: even ask Google to call nearby stores to get product availability for you
insights.locator: You can also see what’s in stock in the area

insights.claim: For live events, AI Mode curates ticket options against a user's stated budget and quantity but sends the user to their preferred platform to finalize the booking, meaning Google is claiming the discovery and comparison layer while leaving checkout with ticketing incumbents for now.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Ticketing platforms keep the transaction but lose demand-shaping control; if Google later closes the loop on checkout, their take rate is exposed.

themes.theme: Canvas and third-party apps rendering inside Search

insights.claim: Canvas in AI Mode can produce a study guide and then build a playable game simulation the user competes against, meaning Search now generates and runs interactive software inside the results surface.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: Search generating disposable apps on demand undercuts the long tail of single-purpose consumer apps and tools; watch app-store download trends in utility categories.

insights.claim: Connecting third-party apps such as Canva to Search lets Canva generate a custom editable design directly within Search results, with the user optionally finishing the work in Canva itself.
insights.speaker: News from Google Team
insights.so_what: This is the two-sided bet for SaaS: Google-scale distribution in exchange for the app becoming a rendered component inside someone else's surface, with the relationship and the prompt owned by Google.
insights.quote: Canva will generate a custom design right in your Search results.
